changes.content: The allowlist is declarative configuration held in the platform repository as environments/{env}/egress-allowlist.auto.tfvars. It is NOT editable at runtime. An allowlist that can be changed without a commit is an allowlist with no audit trail, and the entry that matters is always the one nobody remembers adding.

```text
entry {
  destination  = "<host>"      # the only field the gateway enforces on
  owner        = "<team>"      # PLT-C5 requires a named owner
  reason       = "<why>"       # PLT-C5 requires a stated reason
  adr          = "<ADR id>"    # the decision that authorised it
}
```
Cycle 1 holds exactly one entry, owned by the HarvestLink product unit, reason 'FR-003 FBO verification', authorised by ADR-012.

A denied attempt logs the destination and the calling workload identity and does NOT log the request body — the body of an FBO lookup carries a producer's registration number, and a denial log is the last place that should acquire one. The caller receives a connection refusal it cannot distinguish from the destination being down, which is correct: from identity-service's side both are NoAnswer, and NoAnswer has one defined behaviour.
No TLS interception. The gateway forwards the encrypted stream; it does not hold the destination's certificate chain for inspection purposes and cannot read the payload.

The gateway holds no secrets. It authorises by destination only. Any credential required by a destination is resolved at runtime by the calling workload from the group vault — the gateway never sees it and never proxies authentication.

guardrails.gr-L1-secret-scanner: pass — 0 findings; the component holds no secrets by design
